Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the call this morning. We need a concise mutual action plan (MAP) and a recommended runway that highlights tradeoffs between Hosted, Dedicated, and Private (VPC/on-prem). Procurement wants a clear procurement milestone list (contracts, SOC2 evidence, network review) and an expected go/no-go close date — our CFO is targeting a decision in early October.

Could you send a one-page MAP and a proposed evaluation sprint schedule by EOD Monday? Also flag any blockers that would push us toward Dedicated or Private.

Best,

Hi Alice —

Thanks — attaching an initial MAP (MAP-AcmeHealth-v3.xlsx) and a short decision matrix. High level:
- Week 0–2 (Evaluation): Hosted trial + infra checklist; run your POC prompts against our curated SLO profile.
- Week 2–4 (Security & procurement): SOC2 evidence, network architecture review. If required, run Dedicated sizing exercise in parallel.
- Week 4 (Decision checkpoint): Recommend a go/no-go meeting — target decision by 2026-10-05.

Key blockers that typically push customers to Dedicated/Private:
- Regulatory constraints requiring E2E control over keys or air-gapped processing.
- Extremely tight latency SLOs under consistent high throughput (predictable cost concerns).
- Procurement preferences for fixed-cost reserved capacity.

We can condense the MAP to a single-page PDF; Karthik and Ben are looping in architecture and CSM details.

Attachments: MAP-AcmeHealth-v3.xlsx; SOC2-evidence-summary.pdf

—
Marissa Cole

Subject: Re: Next steps for deployment mode decision and timeline

Marissa / Ben —

Quick notes from infra/solutions perspective:
1) Hosted path (fastest): We can stand up a scoped trial in AWS us-west-2 within 48–72 hours for the POC. We’ll enable prefix caching and request-level KV caching to match their sample workload. Latency profile: 20–80ms median depending on model.
2) Dedicated (reserved): Needs capacity sizing conversation — estimate 2–4 GPUs for their expected concurrency (Ben, can you confirm expected peak concurrent sessions?). Pros: predictable throughput and potential cost savings at scale. Cons: 2–3 week lead time for provisioning in our Dedicated pool.
3) Private (VPC/on-prem): Requires network and KMS integration windows; if they insist on HSM-backed keys or on-prem inference, plan for 6–10 week delivery depending on procurement and network approvals.

I recommend we propose a dual-track MAP: run Hosted trial for immediate validation while starting sizing and procurement conversations for Dedicated if they want committed capacity. Escalate to Private only if their security questionnaire includes non-negotiable on-prem clauses.

Technical attachments: image-deployment-diagram.png (high-level architecture for Hosted vs Dedicated).

Karthik
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
